model_annotation: The plot shows how classification accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and is on a logarithmic scale, with major tick labels at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³, spanning from single-digit co-occurrence values on the left to a few thousand on the right; four sampled x positions are plotted (approximately around 3, 30, 300, and 3000). The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging roughly from 37% to 67%, with labeled ticks at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, and 65 (5-point intervals). The Base series is a black solid line with filled circle markers, increasing from about 38.5% at the leftmost point to about 44% at the rightmost point, with intermediate points near 42% and 44%. The FT series is a blue solid line with downward triangle markers, rising from about 40% to about 47.5%, passing through roughly 43.5% and 46%. The IKE series is a red solid line with upward triangle markers, increasing from about 43% to about 49.5%, with intermediate values around 44.8% and 46.5%. The MEND series is a brown solid line with diamond markers, moving upward from about 44.5% to about 56.5%, with intermediate points near 49% and 54%. The MEMIT series is a purple solid line with pentagon markers, rising from about 44% to about 55%, with intermediate values around 51% and 53%. The ROME series is a green solid line with square markers, increasing from about 51% at the leftmost point to about 66.5% at the rightmost point, with intermediate points near 57% and 62.5%.
